quiz.0.question: What geological environment does Aglianico del Vulture grow in?
quiz.0.options.0: Limestone and clay on the coast
quiz.0.options.1: Ancient volcanic soils on the slopes of Monte Vulture
quiz.0.explanation: Aglianico del Vulture DOCG grows on the ancient volcanic soils of Monte Vulture — an extinct volcano. The volcanic ash-rich basaltic soils give the wine its unique mineral complexity.
quiz.1.question: How long must Aglianico del Vulture Superiore Riserva be aged?
quiz.1.options.1: 5 years (including at least 1 year in bottle)
quiz.1.explanation: Aglianico del Vulture Superiore Riserva requires a minimum of 5 years total ageing — demonstrating the wine's exceptional longevity and seriousness.
quiz.2.question: What is the main difference between Aglianico del Vulture and Taurasi?
quiz.2.options.0: They are made from completely different grape varieties
quiz.2.options.1: Aglianico del Vulture has higher acidity and a more volcanic mineral character; Taurasi is more structured and tannic
quiz.2.options.2: Taurasi is made in the north; Aglianico del Vulture in the south
quiz.2.options.3: Aglianico del Vulture is always sweeter
quiz.2.explanation: Both use Aglianico but on different terroirs: Basilicata's volcanic soils give del Vulture a more volcanic mineral character and higher acidity; Campania's Irpinia hills give Taurasi greater structure.
quiz.3.question: What is Basilicata cuisine's signature spice?
quiz.3.explanation: Basilicata (and neighbouring Calabria) cuisines are defined by peperoncino — chilli pepper — used liberally in sausages, cheeses and sauces, reflecting the region's bold character.
